Taylor: Quick: porting the JS SDK edge example to an SSR worker and hitting TS + bundler grief. Errors mention overload mismatch + generic inference loss.
Nina: paste the error and your tsconfig. Most of these are moduleResolution / types entrypoint problems.
Taylor: errors: 'TS2345: Argument of type "unknown" is not assignable to parameter of type "T"', and 'No overload matches this call to client.invokeTool(...)'. tsconfig: { module: "esnext", moduleResolution: "bundler", target: "es2022", strict: true }.
Rory: bundlers sometimes follow the wrong conditional export and end up loading the CJS runtime, which flips how default exports are seen. That explains some runtime "is not a function" issues.
Kait: also edge runtimes have slightly different AbortController semantics and no Node-style streams. Our retry/auth layers currently assume Node error shapes; that will break in workers.
Taylor: runtime error I saw: 'TypeError: client.run is not a function' until I switched to named import.
Nina: try `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'` instead of default. Default interop is fragile across bundlers.
Taylor: named import fixed runtime. However, TypeScript still strips my generic on `client.chat<{ id: number }>(...)` sometimes when using esbuild bundling for the worker.
Rory: that suggests types resolution differs during bundling. Quick dev workaround: add "skipLibCheck": true to tsconfig to ignore cross-package d.ts mismatches. Not ideal for CI though.
Kait: medium-term: we should expose a dedicated types entry for edge consumers, like "types/edge/index.d.ts", and add an export map so bundlers pick it.
Nina: another idea: simplify overloads into a single generic method `chat<T = unknown>(...)` and provide helper types for strict mode. `unknown` forces explicit narrowing which is safer than `any`.
Taylor: downside: too many `unknown` hurts DX for quickstarts. Maybe keep ergonomic overloads for plain JS, and add a separate strict-typing import path for TS power users.
Rory: also add example tsconfigs in the examples folder: tsconfig.worker.json (moduleResolution: node16/nodeNext), tsconfig.edge.json (moduleResolution: bundler + dom lib), and a tsconfig.strict.json. That helps maintainers and users.
ci-bot: pipeline failed: examples/edge-worker (types check) — https://ci.internal/edge/722
Kait: action items:
- Rory: audit package.json exports and ensure a stable types path for ESM/edge consumers (owner: Rory)
- Nina: draft typings strategy: ergonomic defaults + opt-in strict types, sketch PR (owner: Nina)
- Kait: patch retry/auth to avoid Node-only assumptions and add polyfills guarded by environment checks (owner: Kait)
- Taylor: add a tiny repro in examples/edge-worker with recommended tsconfig and named imports (owner: Taylor)
Taylor: I'll push the repro and link it here. Thanks everyone.
Nina: please ping #devex with repro links. small minimal examples speed fixes a lot. :rocket:
